events.text: An old healer-goddess with milky eyes stops you on the road of stars and puts a thumb on your brow without asking. "Grey at the edges," she says. "You used it like a hammer. I have a little dew from the Moon-Well. It is not given away."

effects.log: She tips your head back and lets one drop fall.

effects.log: She looks at you a long while. "A season of carrying light up my mountain," she says. You carry it.
She shrugs. "It will not get better on its own," she calls after you.

events.text: A pilgrim god at a feast tells the hall about a spring in the far north of heaven where the moon sits in the water all night, and the water heals eyes that have seen too much. Someone at the feast has a flask of it, and is willing to part with it.

effects.log: The flask is cold even in your warm hand.

choices.text: Go north yourself and find the spring

effects.log: It is a hard road and a cold one, even for a god, and the spring is exactly as they said.
It is only a story, probably. Your eye aches all the way back to your domain.

events.text: A blind god of a small domain taps his way into your temple's court and sits down as if invited. "You have a gift and you burned it," he says. "I burned mine too, once. Let me show you how the Moon-Well water is drawn."

effects.log: It takes a whole season and most of your patience. At the turn of it there is dew in the bowl.

choices.text: Make his temple an offering for his trouble

effects.log: He takes the offering for his temple and gives you the bowl.
He goes, smiling, as if he expected nothing else.

events.text: For an age the place where your root was has been a cold hollow, even inside a god's light. Then a hermit god tells you there is a cave in the ice at the top of heaven where a body can be broken and grown again from nothing, if it survives the breaking.

effects.log: You climb.
You will go when you are stronger.

choices.text: You have made your peace with the hollow

effects.log: You thank the hermit and do not go. Some things are allowed to stay lost, even for gods.

events.text: You wake in the long night of heaven with a pain where your root was torn out, a new pain, like a bone trying to set. A healer-god you trust says it plainly: "It wants to grow back. It will burn you out trying, or it will not."

effects.log: You lie down for the long fever, and let it try.

choices.text: Ask the healer to quiet it for now

effects.log: The healer quiets it. It is only sleeping.

choices.text: Ask the healer to quiet it for good

effects.log: The healer does, and the pain goes, and the hope with it.

events.text: An old god who lost a root once, long before your pantheon was raised, finds you. "Mine grew back," he says. "Harder than before. There is a way through the cold falls at the edge of heaven and the fire behind them, and most who take it come out."

effects.log: He walks you to the falls and leaves you there.

choices.text: Ask him to come back in a few years

effects.log: He nods. "I will be here," he says. "Or I will not."

events.text: There is no thunder in heaven for you. Instead, for a whole season, every kindness you ever did comes back as a test: the domain you saved is burning again, the god you forgave asks for everything, the worshippers you answered pray all at once. Heaven is weighing you.

variants: Heaven sends no thunder for a god. It sends your kindnesses back, all in one season: the domain you saved in flames again, the god you forgave asking for everything, every prayer you ever answered rising at once.

For a whole season the old debts of grace come due together. Every worshipper you lifted, every god you spared, comes back to your temple with a heavier need. Heaven is weighing what kind of god you are.

effects.log: {He} listens to the whole strange story and does not laugh once.

choices.text: Say only that you feel it too

effects.log: {He} nods slowly. "Then we will find out," {he} says.

choices.text: Keep the vow quietly, and watch over {him}

effects.log: You say nothing. You keep the vow.

events.text: You stand in front of {npc} in the hall and look at the thread that runs between the two of you: ages of it, warm and frayed, knotted where you quarrelled and made up. It is the strongest thing a god can own. You lift the knife.

effects.log: It goes.
You look back.

events.text: {npc} is laughing with the heralds in the next hall, and you can see the thread from where you sit, bright as a temple wick. You think of every time {he} stood beside you before the gods. Then you cut it.

effects.log: It goes.
You look back.

events.text: "You look strange today, even for a god," {npc} says, and puts a hand on your arm. The hand is warm. In a moment it will be the hand of someone who has never met you.

effects.log: It goes.
You look back.

events.text: You sit in the dark behind your domain and find the oldest life your soul remembers, long before any temple: a house by a river, a mother's voice, a name you were called before every other name. You hold it a moment. Then you cut it away.

effects.log: It goes.
You look back at the dark room.

events.text: The memory you choose is a summer afternoon from a life long before godhood: someone teaching you to swim, laughing at you. It is the best thing you remember. That is why, even for a god, it has to be this one.

effects.log: It goes.
You look back at the dark room.

events.text: You let a whole life go dark, a life from before the light: its friends, its quarrels, the way it ended. It goes out like a lamp in another hall of your temple. The hall is still there. There is no light in it any more.

effects.log: It goes.
You look back at the dark room.

events.text: You find the wish in you to be prayed to: to be looked up at, to be needed, to walk into a hall and have it kneel. It is older than your godhood, and it has been steering more than you knew. You cut it loose.

effects.log: It goes.
You look back at what you were.

events.text: There is a part of you that has always needed someone to say well done, even after the whole Divine Realm began to say it. You thank it for everything it made you do, and you cut it, and the quiet afterward is enormous.

effects.log: It goes.
You look back at what you were.

events.text: You cut away the wanting. Offerings smell of smoke. Praise sounds like words. A beautiful god is a face. It is not unhappy, exactly. It is very clean, like a hall before anyone has prayed in it.

effects.log: It goes.
You look back at what you were.

events.text: An old ferryman hands you his pole without a word, as if the gods had always been expected to take a turn, and steps off the boat onto the bank and closes his eyes. The boat is yours now, and the river, and every soul that waits to cross it.

effects.log: You begin.

choices.text: Think of the ones you left behind, first

effects.log: You think of them, and then you begin.

events.text: The marsh at the edge of the far shore smells of iron and old incense. The souls that sink in it are heavy with what they did, and some of them were gods. You wade in, and your soul opens like a mouth, and you are not ashamed of it.

effects.log: You begin.

choices.text: Think of the ones you left behind, first

effects.log: You think of them, and then you begin.

events.text: You sit down on the shore and stop being a god at all. After a long while you notice that the river has laws, and the marsh has laws, and the grey light has laws, older than any pantheon's, and that you could learn them all if you were patient enough.

effects.log: You begin.

choices.text: Think of the ones you left behind, first

effects.log: You think of them, and then you begin.

events.text: Lanterns on the grey river, a whole line of them, coming downstream against the current. The wardens of the river do not care that you are a god. They have found out what you have been eating, and they have come to take it back out of you.

effects.log: You turn to face them.
You let go of the far shore.

events.text: A warden of the river stands on the bank where you came out of the marsh, pole in hand, and says, "Being prayed to does not make you the river's master. You carry crimes that are not yours. Put them down, or we will make you."

effects.log: You turn to face them.
You let go of the far shore.

events.text: Three wardens this time, in grey with white lanterns. They have no worshippers and want none. They spread out along the bank to cut you off from the door back into your domain.

effects.log: You turn to face them.
You let go of the far shore.

events.text: The ferryman you passed every day for a century is waiting for you, and he is not a ferryman. He is a warden, and while you were being a god he has been counting.

effects.log: You turn to face them.
You let go of the far shore.

events.text: {npc} left a ribbon of {his} robe on a bench of the hall and walked off without it. It is still warm with {his} light. You know exactly what a thing like this is worth, in your craft, even among gods.

effects.log: You keep it.
You take it back to {npc}.

choices.text: Burn it, so nobody can use it

effects.log: You burn it in the brazier and watch until it is ash.

events.text: A servant of {npc}'s temple trades odds and ends at the back door, and among them is a worn glove that was {his}. The servant does not know what it means to a god who works rites.

effects.log: You keep it.
You take it back to {npc}.

events.text: {npc} broke a comb of jade on the road of stars and threw it away. Caught in its teeth are a few strands of {his} hair, still faintly shining. You could leave it in the cloud. You could pick it up.

effects.log: You keep it.
You take it back to {npc}.

events.text: After the feast of the gods {npc} forgets a cup with the mark of {his} mouth still on the rim. Nobody is looking. A cup is a small thing. In your craft, it is not.

effects.log: You keep it.

events.text: {npc}'s old travelling cloak from before {his} godhood, mended many times, turns up among the offerings at a pilgrims' market. {He} must have given it away in a hard age. It still smells of {his} road.

effects.log: You keep it.
You take it back to {npc}.

events.text: A temple child brings you a little carved charm {npc} lost, hoping for a blessing. You can feel {npc} in it the moment it touches your palm: the ages {he} carried it, the worry {he} rubbed into it.

effects.log: You keep it.
You take it back to {npc}.

events.text: The signs in the smoke of your altar said two threads crossing, and here they cross: {npc} steps out of a door of the hall and straight into you, and two gods stand there apologising far longer than the bump deserved.

effects.log: {He} listens with a half smile. "Then I suppose we had better see what it means," {he} says.

choices.text: Say nothing about it, and stay

effects.log: You say nothing about the signs. You stay.
You walk on. You think about {npc} for a long time afterward.

events.text: {npc} sits down beside you at the feast of the gods because every other seat is taken. By the time the dew is poured you have been talking for an hour, and you remember the omen and the two crossed threads.

effects.log: {He} listens with a half smile. "Then I suppose we had better see what it means," {he} says.

events.text: On the road of stars, a sky-barge with a broken oar, and {npc} sitting on the edge of it looking at the oar in despair. You stop to help. You both know, before the oar is mended, that this was meant.

effects.log: {He} listens with a half smile. "Then I suppose we had better see what it means," {he} says.

events.text: {npc} is the one who finds you when you are lost in a fog at the edge of the Sealed Heavens. {He} says {he} was not meant to be out walking today at all, and something made {him} go.

events.text: The first seal opens, and the gold of your domain falls away: you stand in a mountain pass in the snow, inside someone else's armour, long before there were gods of anything. Two hundred men hold the pass behind you. Tomorrow none of them will be alive.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

choices.text: Ask it what it wants you to know

effects.log: It tells you, in its own voice, more than the memory showed.

events.text: The second seal: a war tent, a map, a lamp, in a world far below the light. A young officer argues with you about the order to hold. You tell him an army that runs is a crowd. He salutes. He dies the next morning, holding. Even a god feels it.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

choices.text: Ask it what it wants you to know

effects.log: It tells you, in its own voice, more than the memory showed.

events.text: The third seal: the general's daughter, eight years old, on his knee, asking why he must go. He tells her someone must keep the door. She ties a ribbon to his sword. In your hand, in the Divine Realm, you can feel where it still is.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

events.text: The fourth seal: the last morning at the pass, eleven of them left. The general laughs for the first time in a month, because the enemy has stopped coming. Then the arrows come from the cliffs. Your hall's light seems very far away.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

events.text: The fifth seal: the general does not remember dying. He remembers the sword cold in his hand, and deciding not to let go. That is why he is still here, at a god's side. He was never ordered to stand down. You could order it. You do not.

events.text: The first seal opens, and for a moment there are no gods: only a green riverbank and a girl humming as she washes cloth. The blade was her father's. She hated it, and hummed to it anyway, because it seemed lonely.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

choices.text: Ask it what it wants you to know

effects.log: It tells you, in its own voice, more than the memory showed.

events.text: The second seal: a sick child in a poor house, and the girl with the blade awake all night beside the bed with a cool cloth. She never drew it in anger. She cut bandages with it. Your temples have healed fewer people than she did.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

effects.log: It tells you, in its own voice, more than the memory showed.

events.text: The third seal: bandits at her door. The girl with the blade, who has never fought, stands in the doorway anyway, very frightened. She is still standing there when they leave. A god could learn something from that doorway.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

events.text: The fourth seal: years later, an old woman by the same river, humming to the same blade. She tells it she is sorry it never became a great sword. It hums back that it did not want to be. It is in a god's hand now, and still does not.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

effects.log: It tells you, in its own voice, more than the memory showed.

events.text: The fifth seal: the spirit was never a person. It was the humming, all those years, gathered into the steel until the steel began to hum by itself. Willow was her name. It kept her name, and now a god keeps it too.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

events.text: The first seal opens on a storm over a sea far below heaven, and a woman laughing at the bow of a ship with a blade in her hand and lightning in her hair. She was Stormcrow before the blade was. She would have dared the Throne of Storms itself.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

choices.text: Ask it what it wants you to know

effects.log: It tells you, in its own voice, more than the memory showed.

events.text: The second seal: a hundred duels on a hundred ridges. She wins most of them. The ones she loses, she laughs at too, and comes back stronger. Nobody ever saw her afraid, not even the gods who watched from above, and some did.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

choices.text: Ask it what it wants you to know

effects.log: It tells you, in its own voice, more than the memory showed.

events.text: The third seal: alone by a campfire, she asks the blade if she will ever find someone worth fighting forever. The blade does not answer. It did not know how, then. It is in a god's hand now, and it thinks it might.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

choices.text: Ask it what it wants you to know

effects.log: It tells you, in its own voice, more than the memory showed.

events.text: The fourth seal: the fight she lost for good, on a high ridge in a storm, against something with dragon blood in it. She laughed right to the end. It was the best fight of her life. The blade remembers the joy, and offers it to you.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

choices.text: Ask it what it wants you to know

effects.log: It tells you, in its own voice, more than the memory showed.

events.text: The fifth seal: she did not want to stop. So she went into the blade the way you step through a door, still laughing, to wait for someone who would take her to more fights. She got a god. She is delighted.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

events.text: The first seal opens on a study full of paper, far below any domain: a thin man with ink on his fingers who keeps a sword on the wall and a brush in his hand. He wrote nine books about fighting and fought perhaps four times.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

choices.text: Ask it what it wants you to know

events.text: The second seal: the scholar teaching bored children their letters, and keeping the restless one behind afterward to show her the sword forms, so she will want to read the books about them. Your pantheon's schools could use him.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

events.text: The third seal: his great treatise, eleven years of work, burned by a jealous rival. He sits down that same evening and starts again from the first page. He is almost finished when the fever comes.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

effects.log: It tells you, in its own voice, more than the memory showed.

events.text: The fourth seal: on his sickbed he lays the sword across his knees and whispers into the steel everything he did not get time to write. It takes three nights. It is still in there, in a god's sword, waiting to be read.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

events.text: The fifth seal: he is still writing. Every form you do, even as a god, is a sentence to him. He has corrected your grammar for ages, out of love, and he would very much like a god to finish his book.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

events.text: The first seal opens on a festival far below the light: lanterns, sugar figures, a little one running through the crowd with a blade much too big for it, giggling, chased by someone shouting its name. You almost laugh aloud in the hall.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

events.text: The second seal: a smith's workshop, and a child asleep under the bench in the warm, hugging the sword it was not allowed to touch. The smith covers it with his coat. No god ever did anything kinder.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

events.text: The third seal: hide-and-seek in a big old house. The child hides in the long chest with the sword. Nobody finds it for hours. It is very proud of itself. It is also very hungry.

events.text: The fourth seal: a winter of fever in the town. The child is the last in the house to fall ill. It asks for the sword to hold. It is not frightened. It thinks it is only going to sleep. You were a god already, somewhere, and did not hear.

events.text: The fifth seal: it went into the blade because the blade was the warmest thing in the room. It has forgotten its name. It hides your sandals in the hall so you will come looking. You start looking for its name instead.

events.text: The first seal opens on a cold hall, colder than any the gods keep, and a young man in black kneeling before a master who tells him mercy is a habit, and habits can be broken. He believes it.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

events.text: The second seal: Ashen Fang was a name given, not born. He earns it in a single winter, doing what his master asks. Each deed is easier than the last. That is what frightens him later, and it frightens the god who holds him now.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

events.text: The third seal: once, only once, he spares someone: a child who looks at him and does not run. His master finds out. The punishment is long. He never spares anyone again, and he never stops thinking about the child.

effects.log: You listen to the end, and the blade is quiet in your hand afterward.

events.text: The fourth seal: his own master kills him, in the end, for growing too strong. He goes into the blade to wait, cold and patient, for the day he can face his master on the far shore. A god's hand is a better place to wait.

events.text: The fifth seal: what the spirit never told you. It does not love the dark arts. It loves being stronger than whatever hurt it. Since a god took it up it has begun, slowly, to know the difference.

events.text: "Report," says a voice from the blade at your side, in the middle of the hall of the gods, and you nearly drop it. "Never mind. A god, now? You have still been slacking. Five seals, and I remember every one. Drills at dawn."

effects.log: It settles into your hand as if it had never left.
"Your soul shines the same, every life," it says. "Once it is grown enough, I can see it from anywhere."

events.text: Your new blade starts humming the moment it is in your hand, under the gold sky of the Divine Realm: a tune you have not heard for a lifetime, and know every note of. "I found you," Willow says softly. "Even up here."

effects.log: It settles into your hand as if it had never left.

events.text: The blade in your hand laughs out loud, and the heralds turn to look. "There you are! A god! Do you have any idea how few people are worth fighting? Gods, though. Gods might be. Come on!"

effects.log: It settles into your hand as if it had never left.

events.text: "Ah," says a dry voice from your sword, as if resuming a sentence, in the middle of a feast of the gods. "Where were we. Chapter four. You held your elbow too high then, and I see godhood has not fixed it."

events.text: Your sandals are missing from the door of your temple in the morning, and you laugh out loud before you know why. A small voice in the blade says, "You remembered! You took ages. I hid them somewhere really good this time."

events.text: The blade is cold in your hand, and then it is not. "I waited," says Ashen Fang. "I told myself I would not. A god now. I am finding that you have changed my habits, even across a death."

events.text: At the edge of the Sealed Heavens, where no god goes twice, a broken stele lies half in the light. Words are cut into it that your method has been missing: a fragment of a canticle, older than your pantheon.

choices.text: Read it all at once, before it fades

ok.log: You read it to the end, and the words settle into your method where they belong.

fail.log: It fades before you reach the end. You keep the first half, which is no use to anyone.

choices.text: Copy it slowly onto your own light

effects.log: You copy it, stroke by stroke, until it is part of you. It takes a long time and costs you nothing else.
You leave it. Some other god will find it, or none.

events.text: The heralds have a habit, when a god has done something the halls will not forget: they find a name for it. You hear yours for the first time from two lesser gods on the road of stars who do not know you are behind them.

effects.log: You answer to it.
You let the gods know you are content with the name you have.

events.text: At the feast of the gods the eldest herald stands, lifts a cup of dew, and names you by your deed, as the old custom is. Every god at the table turns to see what you will do with it.

effects.log: You answer to it.
You let the gods know you are content with the name you have.

events.text: Your worshippers have begun to pray to you by a new name: the one the gods use for you now. A priest of your temple asks, carefully, whether the god will answer to it.

effects.log: You answer to it.
You let the gods know you are content with the name you have.
